findings.location: sections/concise/04-themes.tex, second paragraph, first sentence (PDF p. 3): 'The Introit sets that opening note in two half-verses of the long alphabetical psalm on God's law.'
findings.problem: The Introit antiphon is not two half-verses. propers/verified.md records its construction at marginal no. 1602 as 'Verse 137 entire, then the first half of v. 124 only; the second half (et iustificationes tuas doce me) is not sung', and the printed antiphon it collates reads 'Iustus es, Domine, et rectum iudicium tuum: fac cum servo tuo secundum misericordiam tuam' -- one whole verse joined to half of another. The expansive study states it correctly ('Its antiphon joins two verses from different strophes', sections/10-each-element.tex, 'Introit'), so the error was introduced by compression. It is also contradicted by the clause that immediately follows it in the concise, which distinguishes 'verse 137' from 'the first half of verse 124', so the sentence is self-inconsistent as well as false. This is a textual observation about the appointed text in the reader-facing body of a study whose profile makes text control the governing discipline, standing on the first of the two pages the contract requires to be a substantive source-grounded argument.
findings.required_result: The sentence states the antiphon's actual construction -- one entire verse (137) joined to the first half of verse 124 -- as the expansive study and propers/verified.md have it, so that it agrees with the clause that follows it.

findings.location: sections/concise/10-commentary.tex, 'The voice in which this people prays', final paragraph (PDF p. 9): 'The two differ where the beginning lies, Hilary saying ex nobis autem initium est, ut illa perficiat where Augustine gives the whole of it to God'
findings.problem: The expansive study frames the same disagreement with two things the concise drops: that Hilary wrote 'before the controversy with the Pelagians' and that 'Augustine's account is the one on which the priority of grace rests' (sections/40-just-judge-merciful-hearer.tex). research/scope.md 4.11 records both as the controls on this pair -- Hilary wrote c. 364-367, 'his sentence is recorded as his; no later label is put on it', and 'a reading that uses the Introit for grace's priority rests on Augustine'. The concise keeps both witnesses and does not cite Hilary for Augustine's point, so the scope record's binding instruction is met; but a reader of the concise alone meets 'ex nobis autem initium est' as a Doctor's flat teaching on where salvation begins, with nothing to place it historically or doctrinally.
findings.required_result: The sentence carries one of the study's two orienting clauses -- that Hilary wrote before the Pelagian controversy, or that the priority of grace rests on Augustine's account -- so that the reader of the concise meets Hilary's formula with the same frame the expansive study gives it.

findings.location: sections/concise/10-commentary.tex, 'The sevenfold unus, and the division at its last verse', second paragraph (PDF p. 7): 'Chrysostom reads them instead of the one God and Father:'
findings.problem: Read straight, the clause says Chrysostom reads the three phrases in place of the one God and Father, which is the opposite of what he does. The expansive study's corresponding passage is unambiguous: 'St John Chrysostom reads the verse otherwise ... He does not give the three phrases to three Persons. He reads them as three relations of the one God and Father to all things' (sections/30-son-and-lord-of-david.tex). Compression collapsed 'otherwise' and 'as three relations of' into a single 'instead of', and the result is a garden path at the exact point where the concise is distinguishing the two lines of exegesis at Eph 4:6 -- the place research/interpretations.md 2.5 warns must not credit Chrysostom with the distribution.
findings.required_result: The clause says plainly that Chrysostom instead reads the three phrases of the one God and Father, so that 'instead' cannot be taken as governing 'the one God and Father'.

findings.location: sections/concise/01-inventory.tex, the note under the page-1 map (PDF p. 1): 'it has the one oration above and admits no optional text'
findings.problem: The map directly above prints three orations -- Collect, Secret and Postcommunion -- so the note appears to contradict the table it annotates. The rubrical sense intended, that the Mass says a single set of orations with no commemoration, is never stated in the concise; the fact behind it is in the expansive study alone ('The calendar's commemoration of Saints Eustace and Companions on that day gives way to the Sunday, since a Sunday of the second class admits no commemoration but that of a feast of the same class', sections/00-opening.tex). The concise is judged as a document a reader uses without opening the long study, and here that reader is left with an apparent contradiction on page 1.
findings.required_result: The note says what it means without appearing to contradict the map -- that the Mass says one set of orations and admits no commemoration -- or drops the clause.

findings.location: sections/concise/01-inventory.tex, the Gradual row of the page-1 map (PDF p. 1): 'Blessed the nation the Lord chose for his inheritance; the heavens made firm by his word and the spirit of his mouth.'
findings.problem: The respond of Ps 32:12 is 'Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord: the people whom he hath chosen for his inheritance', and the chant's own incipit is Beata gens, cuius est Dominus Deus eorum. The concise's cell drops the first clause and leaves the beatitude resting on the choosing alone. The expansive study's map keeps it ('Blessed the nation whose God is the Lord, the people he chose for his inheritance', sections/00-opening.tex). Nowhere else in the concise is the clause supplied, so the one place its reader is told what the Gradual says omits the half of the verse that states why the nation is blessed -- the half Augustine's Hoc ama, hoc posside and Cassiodorus's inheritance won by blood are both expounding two pages later.
findings.required_result: The Gradual's 'What it says' cell restores 'whose God is the Lord' beside the choosing for an inheritance, as the expansive study's map has it.

observations.location: sections/concise/10-commentary.tex, 'Vows paid, vices cured, and the end this Mass looks to', third paragraph (PDF pp. 9-10)
observations.note: The Secret-to-Preface adjacency is used here as part of the second reading's confession without the bound the expansive study attaches to it at both of its appearances -- 'That adjacency belongs to every Sunday of the second class that uses this Preface' and 'The Preface, finally, is the ordinary Sunday Preface of the season and speaks for every such Sunday' (sections/30-son-and-lord-of-david.tex). The concise does carry the fact, but only in the page-1 note under the map ('Its Preface, of the Most Holy Trinity, is appointed by rubric and is not proper to the day'), nine pages earlier and out of sight of the argument that uses it. Nothing false is asserted, so this is not raised as a finding; it is the one place where the concise's placement of a bound, rather than its presence, is worth a second look.

summary: Cold review of 57-seventeenth-after-pentecost-synthesis (12 physical pages; inventory and the four overview rows settled on page 1, the sole chronology dossier on page 2, Themes and Movement filling pages 3-4, the integrated commentary opening page 5, no overfull boxes and no running-head collision), read against sections/concise/*.tex, the accepted expansive study (00, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 80, 90), propers/verified.md, research/scope.md, research/interpretations.md and the generated chronology annotations. Every Latin and English quotation in the concise traces to the expansive study or the research records, no new source-dependent claim was found, all three controlling claims survive, all six narrow disagreements of sections/50-comparison.tex are preserved (including the lawyer's motive, previously missing), the Rupert/Durandus Luke 14 bound and the Offertory's unsung-verses bound are kept, the chronology cells come from the generated annotations, and the six advisories standing from iteration 2 (SYN-009 through SYN-014) are all cleared. One blocking defect remains: the Themes pages misdescribe the Introit antiphon's construction against the leaf's own text control and against their own next clause. Limits of this review: I did not open the CMAA facsimile, the Migne columns or the other cited printings; source support was checked against propers/verified.md and research/scope.md, which record the sweep, rather than re-performed at the loci.
